title: 1986 AHSME Problem 24
statement:
Let \(p(x)=x^2+bx+c,\) where \(b\) and \(c\) are integers. If \(p(x)\) is a factor of both

\[ x^4+6x^2+25 \]

and

\[ 3x^4+4x^2+28x+5, \] what is \(p(1)?\)

solutions.text:
The common factor \(p(x)\) divides \[ \begin{aligned} &3(x^4+6x^2+25)\\ &\quad{}-(3x^4+4x^2+28x+5)\\ &\qquad=14(x^2-2x+5). \end{aligned} \] Because \(p(x)\) is monic with integer coefficients, Gauss’s lemma implies that it divides \(x^2-2x+5.\) The two polynomials are monic and have the same degree, so \(p(x)=x^2-2x+5.\) Hence \(p(1)=1-2+5=4.\)

Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: A common factor divides every integer linear combination of the two polynomials
